summary: ØRSTED A/S (LEI W9NG6WMZIYEU8VEDOG48, CVR 36213728) is an identifier-confirmed Danish-registered entity with a large multinational subsidiary structure spanning Denmark, the United Kingdom, the United States, and Taiwan, as evidenced by more than twenty GLEIF Level 2 accounting-consolidation relationships. Ownership is indicatively reported by Wikidata (sourced from a 2019 annual report) as approximately 50.1% held by the Ministry of Finance of Denmark, with further indicative shareholdings attributed to Andel Energy (approx. 7.28%), Goldman Sachs (approx. 13.0% per a 2016 source), and Capital Group Companies (approx. 6.0%); state control by the Danish Ministry of Finance is also reported by OpenSanctions, making this a structural indicator of possible state-owned enterprise status that warrants noting. One structural risk signal was identified: the ownership chain reaches three or more corporate layers (GLEIF, medium confidence), meeting the AMLA complexity threshold. Additionally, nine named officers and directors carry possible name-match PEP signals via OpenAleph against the Denmark, Faroe Islands and Greenland PEPs dataset (medium confidence each), but in every case the match is by name only with no corroborating birth date or nationality, so none constitutes a confirmed PEP identification. GLEIF reports a permitted NON_CONSOLIDATING reporting exception for both the direct and ultimate accounting-consolidation parent, meaning no parent entity is disclosed in the LEI record; separately, OpenSanctions data is licensed CC-BY-NC-4.0 and may not be commercially re-used without further clearance.

claims.text: ØRSTED A/S (LEI W9NG6WMZIYEU8VEDOG48, CVR 36213728) is an identifier-confirmed Danish-registered entity.
ØRSTED A/S has a large multinational subsidiary structure, with GLEIF Level 2 accounting-consolidation relationships covering entities in Denmark, the United Kingdom, the United States, and Taiwan.
Wikidata (sourced from a 2019 annual report) indicatively reports the Ministry of Finance of Denmark as holding approximately 50.1% of Ørsted.

OpenSanctions also reports the Ministry of Finance on behalf of the Kingdom of Denmark as holding a shareholding in Ørsted A/S, constituting a structural indicator of possible state-owned enterprise status.
Wikidata indicatively reports Andel Energy as holding approximately 7.28% of Ørsted (sourced from a 2019 annual report), and OpenSanctions separately reports Andel as holding a shareholding.
Wikidata indicatively reports Goldman Sachs as holding approximately 13.0% of Ørsted (sourced from a 2016 annual report).
Wikidata indicatively reports Capital Group Companies as holding approximately 6.0% of Ørsted (sourced from a 2016 annual report).
OpenSanctions also reports Equinor ASA as holding a shareholding in Ørsted A/S.
One structural risk signal was identified: the ownership chain reaches three or more corporate layers, meeting the AMLA complexity threshold (GLEIF, medium confidence).

Nine named officers and directors — Andrew Richard Dingley Brown (næstformand from 2024-03-05), Karl Johnny Hersvik (bestyrelsesmedlem from 2026-04-09), Julia Elizabeth King (bestyrelsesmedlem from 2021-03-01), Julian David Waldron (bestyrelsesmedlem from 2025-04-03), Trond Ødegård Westlie (direktør from 2024-04-01), Rasmus Errboe (adm. dir. from 2025-02-01), Benny Gøbel (bestyrelsesmedlem from 2011-04-12), and Ruchit Majmudar (bestyrelsesmedlem from 2026-04-09) — carry possible name-match PEP signals via OpenAleph against the Denmark, Faroe Islands and Greenland PEPs dataset (medium confidence each), but in every case the match is by name only with no corroborating birth date or nationality, so none constitutes a confirmed PEP identification.
GLEIF reports a permitted NON_CONSOLIDATING reporting exception for both the direct and ultimate accounting-consolidation parent, meaning no parent entity is disclosed in the LEI record.
OpenSanctions data is licensed CC-BY-NC-4.0 and may not be commercially re-used without further clearance.

limitations: No accounting-consolidation parent is disclosed in the GLEIF LEI record due to a permitted NON_CONSOLIDATING reporting exception for both direct and ultimate parent (f1, f2); this is a structural absence, not a data error.

All ownership percentage figures (Ministry of Finance ~50.1%, Andel Energy ~7.28%, Goldman Sachs ~13.0%, Capital Group ~6.0%) are indicative only, sourced from Wikidata referencing annual reports dated 2016 and 2019 — they are not authoritative register data and may be materially out of date (f31, f32, f33, f34).
All nine PEP signals are name-match only with no corroborating identifiers (birth date, nationality); none is a confirmed PEP identification (r4–r12).
OpenSanctions data is licensed CC-BY-NC-4.0; commercial re-use is not permitted under the source licence (g1).
The CVR — Det Centrale Virksomhedsregister was listed as a consulted source but no CVR-specific facts appear in the packet; any findings that might have been drawn from that register are absent.
Wikirate was listed as a consulted source but no Wikirate-specific facts appear in the packet.

risks.label: No parent in GLEIF (permitted reporting exception)
risks.rationale: No accounting-consolidation parent is reported to GLEIF: NON_CONSOLIDATING for the direct and ultimate parent (its controlling legal entities are not subject to preparing consolidated financial statements). Structural context, not a risk finding — these are permitted exceptions under the LEI ROC policy, and GLEIF Level 2 records accounting consolidation, not beneficial ownership.

risks.label: Outside EU/EEA
risks.rationale: Ownership chain reaches jurisdictions outside the EU/EEA: GB, TW, US-AZ, US-DE. Structural context, not a risk finding — neither the AMLA CDD RTS nor AMLR Annex III treats non-EU status as a risk factor in itself. Contributes to AMLA Article 12(1) condition (b) only where it appears on the layered ownership path.

risks.label: Complex ownership layers
risks.rationale: Ownership chain has 3 corporate layers (AMLA threshold: ≥3).
